title: Set up your Rust workshop
summary: Install a reproducible toolchain, read a Cargo project, and make the first edit.

title: Values, functions, and control flow
summary: Express decisions with types, functions, matching, and explicit numeric boundaries.

title: Ownership, places, and moves
summary: Track who owns a value and why passing it can make its old location unavailable.

title: Borrowing and reborrowing
summary: Reason about permitted access over time instead of treating references as spare owners.

title: Strings, slices, and collections
summary: Use UTF-8 deliberately and choose ownership at collection boundaries.

title: Structs, enums, and useful states
summary: Make domain distinctions visible without building an elaborate type architecture.

title: Errors as part of the interface
summary: Distinguish malformed input, missing values, broken assumptions, and operational failure.

title: Stage build: the first event counter
summary: Combine control flow and borrowed text into a small working program.

title: Lifetimes describe relationships
summary: Design borrowed results without pretending annotations extend storage.

title: Traits where abstraction earns its place
summary: Use standard interfaces, associated types, and dispatch intentionally.

title: Iterators and closures without hidden ownership
summary: Read item types, captures, laziness, and short-circuiting results.

title: Stage build: a bounded streaming library
summary: Separate parsing from I/O and enforce memory limits before input grows.

title: Cargo, modules, and dependency boundaries
summary: Read the actual workspace, feature graph, lockfile, and release configuration.

title: Tests, diagnostics, and complementary tools
summary: Test contracts and failures, and use compiler output without inventing it.

title: Interior mutability and shared ownership
summary: Distinguish reference counts, runtime borrowing, and synchronization.

title: Threads, Send, and Sync
summary: Transfer or borrow work safely while keeping completion and failure explicit.

title: Channels, locks, and shutdown
summary: Choose ownership transfer or shared state, and reason about waiting.

title: Atomics and memory ordering
summary: Separate an indivisible counter update from publication of other data.

title: Futures before runtimes
summary: Understand polling, wakeups, state machines, and what await does not promise.

title: Tokio tasks, blocking, and cancellation
summary: Use a runtime with bounded queues, explicit task results, and deliberate shutdown.

title: Pin and async trait boundaries
summary: Understand address-sensitive values and stable alternatives to native async dyn dispatch.

title: Stage build: an async ingestion pipeline
summary: Keep one owner of the aggregate while producers hand over bounded work.

title: Unsafe boundaries and soundness
summary: Audit one small abstraction with explicit invariants, edge cases, and Miri.

title: Measure performance and resource use
summary: Build a reproducible experiment before changing allocation, dispatch, or build profiles.

title: Stable Rust and the horizon
summary: Read current initiatives without turning goals, experiments, or compiler limitations into stable promises.

title: FFI, serialization, and public contracts
summary: Design boundaries where Rust types alone cannot validate the other side.

title: Capstone: ship Fieldnotes
summary: Assemble the tested parser and bounded reader into an installable command-line product.

title: Release, maintain, and keep learning
summary: Review a public API, reproduce a release, and maintain the course's evidence.
